# Server-side push delivery

[English](push.md) | [日本語](../../../ja/api/v1/push.md) | [Français](../../../fr/api/v1/push.md) | [中文](../../../api/v1/push.md)

<!-- Generated by npm run docs:localize; edit docs/i18n/translations.json. -->

Core sends new notifications to enabled NTFY, BARK, or MACOS_NOTIFICATION targets independently of the main model. DISPATCHED/dispatched_at means the channel API accepted the request; client presentation and reads are reported separately. See [push-service](../../../../src/pi_secretary/src/push-service.ts) and [push-transport](../../../../src/pi_secretary/src/push-transport.ts).

## Create a target

Use local-owner authentication and the `/api/v1` prefix. First create a disabled target with `POST push-targets`:

```json
{
  "request_id": "11111111-1111-4111-8111-111111111111",
  "name": "Phone",
  "kind": "NTFY",
  "endpoint": "https://ntfy.sh",
  "enabled": false,
  "quiet_hours": {"timezone": "Asia/Hong_Kong", "start": "22:00", "end": "08:00"}
}
```

The receipt links the target ID; GET push-targets/{id} reads configuration. Update by POSTing the same path with the full configuration, a new request_id, and current expected_revision. At most 20 targets are allowed; the delivery worker does not change target revision.

endpoint is an exact HTTP(S) origin, such as `https://ntfy.example.com`, with no trailing slash, path, query, fragment, or userinfo; MACOS_NOTIFICATION uses null. quiet_hours is null or an IANA timezone with distinct HH:mm start/end times; midnight crossings and daylight saving use local time. Remote targets use HTTPS; previews travel through the configured service and its downstream notification channels.

## Configure credentials and enable delivery

Create push-secrets in the Core data directory with mode 0700. Write `<target UUID>.json`, owned by the Core user, mode 0600, at most 8 KiB; the path must be a regular file. Credential format:

```json
{"topic":"replace-with-private-topic","token":"replace-with-access-token"}
```

The example above is for NTFY; services allowing anonymous publishing may omit token. BARK uses `{"device_key":"replace-with-device-key"}`. Alternatively, before startup set `SECRETARY_PUSH_<UUID in uppercase with hyphens replaced by underscores>` to the same JSON. Environment values take precedence over files. Credentials never enter public configuration.

Enable the target after writing credentials. Enabling creates a new generation at the configuration transaction watermark and sends notifications created afterward. Disabling cancels pending items. Re-enabling or changing kind/endpoint creates a new generation; changing name or quiet hours preserves the backlog. In-flight requests still record actual outcomes; failures after disabling do not retry.

Credential files are reread for each send. Rotate using an atomic rename of a same-directory temporary file with mode 0600; environment credentials refresh on restart. When changing a topic/device-key destination, disable, change credentials, then enable so old backlog remains in its original generation. Missing, malformed, or incorrectly permissioned secrets return SECRET_UNAVAILABLE; queries retain stable error codes.

## Delivery and recovery

Each send times out after 10 seconds, caps responses at 8 KiB, rejects redirects, and records acceptance only after validating the channel success response. NTFY sends topic/message/title and an optional Bearer token; BARK sends device_key/body/title; macOS uses the local osascript notification interface.

After the first send, up to three retries wait 30 seconds, 2 minutes, and 10 minutes. Interrupted attempts count against the four-attempt budget; an interrupted final attempt becomes FAILED/INTERRUPTED. Restart restores notifications and dispatches with their budgets and rate accounting. A crash after channel acceptance but before local persistence may duplicate delivery.

Each target allows at most three attempts per rolling minute, including failures. Quiet hours pause attempts. Once the window ends or a rate slot opens, backlog is batched in groups of at most 100; retries retain original batch membership. Previews contain at most 200 Unicode characters plus a prompt to view in the client; JSON notifications extract only text.

## Queries and sync

GET push-targets and push-targets/{id} return configuration. GET push-dispatches filters by target_id and state, default 30, maximum 100, with filter-bound cursors. Details include notification/target IDs, generation, batch, attempt history, next time, error code, and acceptance time. States are PENDING/SENDING/DISPATCHED/FAILED/CANCELLED. Targets and dispatch records enter sync/changes and sync/stream; queries are read-only.

## Current limitations

- Records remain queryable after retries are exhausted; no resend API exists for terminal failures yet.
- Actual macOS banner display depends on system permissions; real phone-delivery acceptance belongs to portable terminal #11.
- Quiet hours and retries require Core to run; settle does not wait for future deadlines.
